charts.title: Global dairy and meat prices
charts.question: Are international dairy and meat markets strengthening or easing?
charts.description: FAO monthly commodity price indices over the last ten years.
charts.basis: International commodity price index, with the 2014–2016 average equal to 100.
charts.sourceTitle: FAO Food Price Index monthly data
charts.note: FAO can revise previously published values. The dashboard retains the latest values in the current official file.

series.label: Dairy
series.definition: International quotations for butter, cheese, skim milk powder, and whole milk powder.

series.label: Meat
series.definition: International quotations for bovine, ovine, pig, and poultry meat.

charts.title: U.S. all-milk price
charts.question: How has the national milk-price environment changed?
charts.description: Monthly average price received by U.S. producers for all milk at the average milk-fat test.
charts.basis: National dollars per hundredweight. This is an industry average, not an individual producer’s milk check.
charts.sourceTitle: USDA ERS U.S. dairy situation at a glance
charts.note: Monthly prices are national averages and do not include regional basis, component premiums, deductions, or individual farm costs.

series.label: All-milk price
series.definition: Average price received by U.S. producers for all milk sold during the month.

charts.title: U.S. milk production
charts.question: Is the national milk supply expanding or contracting?
charts.description: Quarterly U.S. milk production over the last ten years, including the recurring seasonal pattern.
charts.basis: National production in millions of pounds. Quarter-to-quarter comparisons are seasonal; year-over-year change is the cleaner signal.
charts.sourceTitle: USDA ERS quarterly U.S. milk production data
charts.note: Use year-over-year change to separate underlying supply movement from normal seasonal production patterns. Quarterly totals are not directly comparable with monthly totals.

series.label: Milk production
series.definition: Total milk produced in the United States during the reporting quarter.

charts.title: U.S. retail beef values
charts.question: How quickly are national beef values moving at retail?
charts.description: Monthly national Choice and all-fresh beef retail values over the available two-year window.
charts.basis: National average dollars per pound of retail equivalent, converted from the source series reported in cents per pound.
charts.sourceTitle: USDA ERS Choice beef values and spreads
charts.note: The source combines BLS retail data with USDA AMS livestock and wholesale market reporting. Values are national averages.

series.label: Choice beef
series.definition: Retail-equivalent value for Choice-grade beef from a standardized animal and cutting profile.

series.label: All-fresh beef
series.definition: BLS-derived average retail value for fresh beef sold to U.S. consumers.

charts.title: U.S. cattle supply
charts.question: What is changing in the domestic cattle base?
charts.description: July 1 inventory and annual calf-crop estimates for 2025 and 2026.
charts.basis: USDA national estimates in millions of animals. Beef cows are a July 1 inventory; calf crop covers the calendar year.
charts.note: July cattle inventory reporting was not conducted in 2024. No value is interpolated for that missing release.

series.label: Beef cows
series.definition: Cows and heifers that have calved and are kept for beef production, estimated on July 1.

series.label: Calf crop
series.definition: Calves born during the calendar year, reported as USDA’s annual national estimate.

series.label: Cattle on feed
series.definition: Cattle being fed a concentrated ration for slaughter in U.S. feedlots on the reporting date.
